prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: In her account of one season, an ornithologist wrote that a string of early storms had ______ the geese's migration.

worlds.passage: Each autumn several thousand snow geese fly some three thousand kilometers from the northern tundra to coastal marshes, and ordinarily the whole population lifts off within a few days of one another in mid-October. That year the storms came one after another, and the geese flew only in the calm gaps between them, a few flocks at a time. Banded birds were still leaving the tundra in late November, and counters on the marshes logged arrivals across seven weeks instead of one, ending with roughly their usual total. In her account of one season, an ornithologist wrote that a string of early storms had ______ the geese's migration.
worlds.explanation: Flying only in calm gaps, a few flocks at a time, the geese left and arrived over seven weeks instead of together, so the storms "staggered" the migration. "Truncated" fails because the birds reached the marshes; "spurred" fails because some were still leaving in late November, later than usual; "swelled" fails because the total was roughly the usual one.

truncated.quote: counters on the marshes logged arrivals
truncated.why: The geese reached their destination, so the trip was not cut short.

spurred.quote: still leaving the tundra in late November
spurred.why: Birds leaving weeks late were held back, not hurried.

swelled.why: The number of birds did not grow.

worlds.passage: Each autumn several thousand snow geese fly some three thousand kilometers from the northern tundra to coastal marshes, and ordinarily the whole population lifts off within a few days of one another in mid-October. That year the flocks set off together on their usual date, after the first storms had already glazed the southern prairies with ice. Banded birds turned up all winter on a chain of open lakes halfway along the route, and counters on the marshes, who usually log thousands of arrivals, logged almost none at all. In her account of one season, an ornithologist wrote that a string of early storms had ______ the geese's migration.
worlds.explanation: The geese left on time but spent the winter on lakes halfway along the route and never reached the marshes, so the storms "truncated" the migration. "Staggered" fails because the flocks set off together; "spurred" fails because they left on their usual date; "swelled" fails because almost no birds arrived at the marshes.

staggered.why: A shared departure was not spread out over time.

spurred.why: Geese leaving at the normal time were not hurried by the storms.

swelled.why: Nothing suggests more birds than usual; the marshes saw almost none.

worlds.passage: Each autumn several thousand snow geese fly some three thousand kilometers from the northern tundra to coastal marshes, and ordinarily the whole population lifts off within a few days of one another in mid-October. "Staggered" fails because the flocks left within hours of one another; "truncated" fails because they reached the marshes; "swelled" fails because the total was nearly the usual one.

worlds.passage: Each autumn several thousand snow geese fly some three thousand kilometers from the northern tundra to coastal marshes, and ordinarily the whole population lifts off within a few days of one another in mid-October. That year the population lifted off on schedule, while the storms, sweeping in from the west, scattered a separate population that nests far to the west. Counters on the marshes, logging arrivals over the usual single week, found nearly twice their usual total, many of the birds wearing bands from western colonies. In her account of one season, an ornithologist wrote that a string of early storms had ______ the geese's migration.
worlds.explanation: Birds blown in from a western population joined the flight, and nearly twice the usual number arrived, so the storms "swelled" the migration. "Staggered" fails because arrivals came in the usual single week; "truncated" fails because the birds reached the marshes; "spurred" fails because the population left on schedule.
